correctness.rationale: For each exponent partition, the exact maximum abundancy is obtained by assigning its exponents in all distinct ways to the smallest available primes. Every total multiplicity below eight has maximum below four. At multiplicity eight only three partitions survive; an exact monotone branch bound makes all three prime-assignment searches finite and leaves only \(2^3\cdot3^2\cdot5\cdot7\cdot13\), whose divisor sum is exactly four times itself.

value.rationale: Quadriperfect numbers remain incompletely classified. Total prime-factor multiplicity is a natural structural invariant complementary to the classical distinct-prime count. Determining its exact minimum and the unique equality case gives a complete first layer rather than a bounded computation.
